memory_boundary: Memory-only structural leads for source discovery. No external search, Evidence search, broker ranking, charter-party clause verification, arbitration lookup or jurisdiction-specific legal conclusion was used.

leads.memory: Owner, disponent owner/operator, charterer and shipbroker can occupy distinct commercial roles; the party negotiating employment of a vessel is not necessarily the registered owner or the party operating every technical function.

Chartering markets are organized around cargo orders and vessel positions circulated through broker networks or direct relationships; timing, information quality and exclusivity affect which opportunities are genuinely actionable.

Negotiation proceeds through offers/counteroffers and can remain conditional on subjects or approvals after headline economics appear agreed; a commercially discussed deal is not always a fully unconditional fixture.

A fixture recap can crystallize agreed main terms before a full charter-party document is finalized, making recap/fixture time an important contract-state and known-time boundary for historical replay.

Under a voyage charter the owner generally prices a defined cargo/voyage employment while retaining much vessel-operating exposure; realized revenue depends on voyage time, port time, fuel and contract time-allocation mechanisms rather than the freight rate alone.

A time charter shifts commercial employment for a period while the owner normally retains technical/navigation responsibilities; hire, bunkers, trading orders and off-hire rules create a different economic state machine from a voyage charter.

Notice of Readiness is a key voyage-charter transition because contractual laytime does not simply equal physical arrival time; readiness, location and acceptance/timing records can determine when time starts counting.

Port agents, master/terminal records and Statements of Facts create a timestamped evidence trail for arrival, berthing, cargo operations, stoppages and completion; these records underpin later laytime and delay calculations.

Allowed laytime, exclusions/interruptions and actual time used are reconciled after operations; demurrage or despatch can materially change voyage economics, so port delay is partly a contract-allocation question rather than only an operational metric.

Under time charter, certain periods may cease to earn hire depending on contract-defined circumstances; off-hire analysis therefore links operational events, causation, duration and evidence to realized owner revenue.

Time-charter delivery/redelivery often requires bunker quantity and price accounting plus responsibility for consumption/procurement during the charter, linking the P005 bunker chain directly to charter economics.

Commercial voyage instructions from charterers interact with the master's navigation/safety authority and owner's technical obligations; this boundary is operationally important when orders, port suitability, speed or routing create tension.

After fixture, operators and claims/chartering staff administer notices, invoices, supporting records, commissions, hire/freight payments, laytime/off-hire claims and settlement correspondence; the commercial transaction persists well beyond the fixture timestamp.

The atlas index-semantics warning extends further: a published rate/index, a negotiated fixture rate and the finally realized voyage/time-charter economics are distinct objects and should never be substituted for one another.
P008 port-call timestamps acquire contractual meaning in P012 because arrival, NOR, berth, cargo-operation and completion times can drive laytime, delay and claims calculations.

P005 owner/charterer bunker allocation should be modeled through the charter state: procurement responsibility, consumption, quantity at delivery/redelivery and off-spec consequences can fall differently across contracts.

The atlas counterparty-risk mechanism includes unpaid freight/hire, disputed deductions, security and settlement delays; contract administration is one path by which solvency becomes operating cash-flow risk.
The atlas already notes specialized long-term versus spot contracting in LNG and other markets; P012 does not repeat that market-structure lead.
The general requirement to preserve when information became knowable already exists in the atlas; P012 only applies it specifically to fixture, recap and time records.

reviewed_no_specific_memory.reason: Exact forms, riders, clause wording and edition histories require primary contract/Evidence work.
Current or historical rankings and exact commissions are uneven and source-dependent.
Legal outcomes are claim-specific and cannot be inferred from blind memory.
Specific disputes, payment defaults and settlement facts require source-scoped Evidence.

method_observation.observation: Recall stays high-yield when a fixture is followed through conditional agreement, operational timestamps, contractual time allocation and settlement. It degrades when probing turns into clause libraries, broker rankings or arbitration anecdotes.
